Ethinylestradiol and CYP3A4 Metabolism: Ethinylestradiol can influence the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, potentially increasing or decreasing their effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Norgestimate and Metformin: Norgestimate reduces the efficacy of metformin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is recommended. 3. Ethinylestradiol and Metformin: Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of metformin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Metronidazole and Ethinylestradiol: Metronidazole reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Mifepristone and Norgestimate: Mifepristone decreases the effects of norgestimate through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraception is recommended, and monitoring is advised. 6. Ethinylestradiol and Mexiletine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 7. Ethinylestradiol and Midazolam: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of midazolam by reducing its metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 8. Ethinylestradiol and Benzodiazepines: Ethinylestradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, leading to increased serum concentrations. Monitoring is recommended. 9. Ethinylestradiol and Mifepristone: Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraception is recommended, and monitoring is advised. 10. Minocycline and Ethinylestradiol: Minocycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 11. Mitotane and Ethinylestradiol: Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring and potential dosage adjustments are necessary. 12. Momelotinib and Ethinylestradiol: Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol due to plasma protein binding competition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 13. Moxifloxacin and Ethinylestradiol: Moxifloxacin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 14. Nafcillin and Ethinylestradiol: Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 15. Nemolizumab and Norgestimate/Ethinylestradiol: Nemolizumab decreases the levels of norgestimate and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 16. Neomycin and Ethinylestradiol: Neomycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 17. Siltuximab and Ethinylestradiol: Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated during infection or inflammation. Caution is advised when coadministered with CYP substrates with a narrow therapeutic index. 18. Ethinylestradiol and Nicardipine/Nilotinib: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of nicardipine and nilotinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 19. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir and Ethinylestradiol: These drugs decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by increasing its metabolism. Additional nonhormonal contraception is recommended for the remainder of the cycle. 20. Nitrofurantoin and Ethinylestradiol: Nitrofurantoin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 21. Ethinylestradiol and Olanzapine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of olanzapine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 22. Otesecozole and Ethinylestradiol: Otesecozole, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase the effects and toxicity of BCRP substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 23. Paromomycin and Ethinylestradiol: Paromomycin reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 24. Penicillin G/VK and Ethinylestradiol: Penicillin G increases the metabolism of ethinylestradiol, while Penicillin VK alters intestinal flora, reducing its levels or effects. Monitoring is recommended. 25. Pioglitazone and Ethinylestradiol: Pioglitazone decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring is advised. 26. Posaconazole and Ethinylestradiol: Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 27. Quinupristin/Dalfopristin and Ethinylestradiol: These drugs increase the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 28. Ethinylestradiol and Ramelteon/Rasagiline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ramelteon and rasagiline by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 29. Ribociclib and Ethinylestradiol: Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 30. Romidepsin and Ethinylestradiol: Romidepsin decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol through receptor binding competition. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Ethinylestradiol and Ropinirole: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of ropinirole by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 32. Rucaparib and Ethinylestradiol: Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Rufinamide and Ethinylestradiol: Rufinamide decreases the effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 34. Ethinylestradiol and Selegiline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of selegiline by inhibiting its N-demethylation. Monitoring is advised. 35. Ethinylestradiol and Somapacitan/Somatrogon/Somatropin: Ethinylestradiol reduces the effects of these growth hormone analogs by decreasing serum IGF-1 response. Higher GH doses may be required. 36. Stiripentol and Ethinylestradiol: Stiripentol, a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, may alter the effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 37. Sulfadiazine/Sulfamethoxazole/Sulfisoxazole and Ethinylestradiol: These drugs reduce the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 38. Tacrolimus and Ethinylestradiol: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 39. Tazemetostat and Ethinylestradiol: Tazemetostat decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol, while ethinylestradiol increases the levels of tazemetostat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 40. Tecovirimat and Ethinylestradiol: Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol. Monitoring is advised. 41. Teriflunomide and Ethinylestradiol: Teriflunomide increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unknown mechanism. Monitoring is recommended. 42. Tetracycline and Ethinylestradiol: Tetracycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 43. Ethinylestradiol and Theophylline: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of theophylline by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 44. Tigecycline and Ethinylestradiol: Tigecycline reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 45. Ethinylestradiol and Tinidazole: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 46. Ethinylestradiol and Tizanidine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tizanidine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitoring for adverse effects such as hypotension or bradycardia is advised. 47. Ethinylestradiol and Tolterodine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 48. Ethinylestradiol and Triazolam: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of triazolam by reducing its metabolism. Monitoring is advised. 49. Trimethoprim and Ethinylestradiol: Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but monitoring is recommended. 50. Ethinylestradiol and Ursodiol: Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of ursodiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitoring is recommended. 51. Vadadustat and Ethinylestradiol: Vadadustat increases the levels of ethinylestradiol by increasing BCRP substrate exposure. Monitoring for adverse effects is advised. 52. Ethinylestradiol and Valoctocogene Roxaparvovec: Ethinylestradiol may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when combined with valoctocogene roxaparvovec. Monitoring and consideration of alternative medications are recommended. 53. Ethinylestradiol and Valproic Acid: Ethinylestradiol decreases the levels of valproic acid by increasing its elimination, potentially leading to increased seizure frequency. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 54. Voriconazole and Ethinylestradiol: Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 55. Norgestimate and Warfarin: Norgestimate increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified mechanism. Monitoring is advised. 56. Acetazolamide and Ethinylestradiol: Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 57. Ethinylestradiol and Amitriptyline/Amoxapine: Ethinylestradiol may alter the effects of tricyclic antidepressants, increasing plasma concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance is unknown. 58. Anastrozole and Ethinylestradiol: Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 59. Ethinylestradiol and Antipyrine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of antipyrine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 60. Ethinylestradiol and Asenapine: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of asenapine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown. 61. Ethinylestradiol and Clarithromycin: Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown.
